questions.stem: In vasectomy, a small part of which structure is removed or tied up?
questions.explanation: Vasectomy is a surgical method of sterilisation in males. A small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up through a small incision on the scrotum, so sperms cannot be carried to the urethra and the semen.

optionRationale.2: The epididymis is not cut in vasectomy.
optionRationale.3: The urethra carries both urine and semen and is not cut.
optionRationale.4: The ureter carries urine from the kidney.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a natural method of contraception?
questions.explanation: Natural methods work on the principle of avoiding the chance of ovum and sperm meeting. Periodic abstinence, withdrawal and lactational amenorrhoea are natural methods. Copper T, pills and diaphragms involve devices or drugs.

optionRationale.1: Copper T is an intra-uterine device.
optionRationale.4: A diaphragm is a barrier device.

questions.stem: Emergency contraceptives are effective if used within how many hours of unprotected coitus?
questions.explanation: Administration of progestogens, progestogen-oestrogen combinations or IUDs within 72 hours of unprotected coitus has been found to be very effective as emergency contraception, and it can prevent a possible pregnancy.

optionRationale.1: 12 hours is too short a period.
optionRationale.2: 7 days is longer than the effective period.

questions.objective: State the time limit for emergency contraception

questions.stem: Diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults are
options: devices placed in the uterus to prevent implantation
reusable barriers that cover the cervix
questions.explanation: These are barriers made of rubber that are inserted into the female reproductive tract to cover the cervix. They block the entry of sperms into the uterus, and they can be used again after cleaning.

optionRationale.1: Devices in the uterus are IUDs.

questions.stem: Hormonal implants and injections used by females act on the same principle as
questions.explanation: Progestogens or progestogen-oestrogen combinations given as injections or implants under the skin have a mode of action similar to that of pills, but they are effective for a much longer period.

optionRationale.1: Copper T releases copper ions that suppress sperm motility.
optionRationale.4: Tubectomy blocks the passage of the ovum surgically.

questions.stem: Couples practising periodic abstinence avoid coitus from day 10 to day 17 of the menstrual cycle because
options: the endometrium is shed in this period
ovulation is expected during this period and chances of fertilisation are very high
oestrogen level is lowest in this period
questions.explanation: Ovulation occurs around the middle of the cycle, so on days 10 to 17 the chances of fertilisation are very high. Avoiding coitus in this fertile period is therefore used to prevent pregnancy.

optionRationale.1: Menstruation occurs in the first few days of the cycle.
optionRationale.2: Shedding of the endometrium is menstruation, at the start of the cycle.

questions.stem: A woman with a regular 28-day cycle practises periodic abstinence from day 10 to day 17, both days included. On how many days of the cycle is the couple not abstaining?
questions.explanation: Counting days 10 to 17 with both included gives 8 days of abstinence, since 17 − 10 + 1 = 8. The remaining days of the 28-day cycle are therefore 28 − 8 = 20 days.

optionRationale.3: 8 is the number of days of abstinence.

questions.stem: A woman has blocked fallopian tubes but produces normal ova, and her husband is fertile. Which of the following is the most suitable assisted technique?
options: IVF followed by embryo transfer into the uterus
questions.explanation: With blocked tubes, fertilisation cannot occur in the body, so ova are fertilised in vitro and the embryo is placed in the uterus. GIFT and IUI depend on functioning fallopian tubes, and tubectomy is a method of sterilisation, not a treatment.

optionRationale.1: GIFT places gametes in the fallopian tube, which is blocked.
optionRationale.3: IUI needs the ovum to travel through an open tube.
optionRationale.4: Tubectomy is a contraceptive method, not a treatment.

questions.objective: Choose an ART for tubal blockage

questions.stem: Which pair of sexually transmitted infections is caused by viruses?
questions.explanation: Genital herpes and hepatitis-B are caused by viruses. Gonorrhoea, syphilis and chlamydiasis are caused by bacteria, so each of the other pairs contains at least one bacterial disease, which is treated with antibiotics.

optionRationale.1: Both gonorrhoea and syphilis are bacterial.
optionRationale.2: Both syphilis and chlamydiasis are bacterial.
optionRationale.4: Gonorrhoea is bacterial, so this pair is mixed.

questions.stem: Match the method in List-I with its mode of action in List-II.
questions.explanation: A condom is a barrier. Copper T releases copper ions that suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity. Tubectomy blocks the fallopian tubes of the female, and vasectomy blocks the vas deferens of the male.

optionRationale.2: This pairs 'Condom' with 'Release of copper ions that suppress sperm motility', which describes 'Copper T'.
optionRationale.3: This pairs 'Tubectomy' with 'Cutting or tying the vas deferens', which describes 'Vasectomy'.
optionRationale.4: This pairs 'Condom' with 'Cutting or tying the fallopian tubes', which describes 'Tubectomy'.

questions.objective: Match contraceptive methods with their actions

right: I. Barrier that prevents entry of semen
II. Release of copper ions that suppress sperm motility
III. Cutting or tying the fallopian tubes
IV. Cutting or tying the vas deferens

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Coitus interruptus is a highly reliable method with no chance of failure.
Reason (R): In this method the male withdraws his penis from the vagina just before ejaculation so as to avoid insemination.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: R correctly describes coitus interruptus. It is a natural method, but pre-ejaculatory fluid may contain sperms and withdrawal may fail, so the chance of failure is not zero. A is false and R is true.

optionRationale.1: A is false, so both cannot be true.
optionRationale.2: A is false, so both cannot be true.
optionRationale.3: R is true, so this option is wrong.

questions.objective: Evaluate the reliability of coitus interruptus

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Diaphragms and cervical caps are barrier methods of contraception.
Reason (R): Spermicidal creams, jellies and foams are usually used along with these barriers to increase their contraceptive efficiency.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Diaphragms and cervical caps cover the cervix, so A is true. Spermicidal creams, jellies and foams are used along with them to increase efficiency, so R is also true, but R does not explain why they are barriers.

optionRationale.1: R does not explain why they are barriers.
optionRationale.4: A is true and R is true.

questions.stem: Match the device in List-I with its type in List-II.
questions.explanation: The Lippes loop is a non-medicated IUD. Multiload 375 is a copper-releasing IUD, and LNG-20 is a hormone-releasing IUD. The diaphragm is a barrier method that covers the cervix of the female.

optionRationale.2: This pairs 'Lippes loop' with 'Copper-releasing IUD', which describes 'Multiload 375'.
optionRationale.3: This pairs 'LNG-20' with 'Barrier covering the cervix', which describes 'Diaphragm'.
optionRationale.4: This pairs 'Lippes loop' with 'Hormone-releasing IUD', which describes 'LNG-20'.

questions.objective: Match contraceptive devices with their types

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about sexually transmitted infections.
A. Hepatitis-B and HIV can also be transmitted by sharing injection needles.
B. Avoiding sex with multiple partners and using condoms help prevent STIs.
C. Gonorrhoea and syphilis are caused by viruses.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Hepatitis-B and HIV are also transmitted through shared needles and infected blood. Having a single partner and using condoms reduces the risk. Gonorrhoea and syphilis are bacterial, not viral, so C is wrong.

optionRationale.2: C is wrong, since both are bacterial.
optionRationale.3: C is wrong, and A is correct.
optionRationale.4: C is wrong, so not all three are correct.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about assisted reproductive technologies.
A. In IVF, fertilisation takes place outside the body in conditions almost similar to those in the body.
B. Embryos with more than 8 blastomeres can be transferred into the uterus.
C. In ZIFT, an ovum from a donor is transferred into the fallopian tube.
D. In ICSI, a sperm is injected directly into the ovum.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: IVF is fertilisation in vitro, embryos with more than 8 blastomeres go to the uterus, and ICSI injects a sperm into the ovum. Transfer of a donor ovum into the fallopian tube is GIFT, not ZIFT, so C is wrong.

optionRationale.1: D is also correct, so this option is incomplete.
optionRationale.2: C is wrong, and A is correct.
optionRationale.3: C is wrong, so not all four are correct.
